The canonical string is METHOD|PATH|TIMESTAMP|NONCE|PAYLOAD_MODE|BODY_HASH|USER_ID; use the URL-decoded path without the query string. Timestamps are Unix seconds with a 300-second tolerance. info.description:
After pairing, an app can call the device API within the feature permissions the current user and your CODE27 already have, including reading user data and controlling your CODE27. Access isn't granted per app, so consider how each app you use stores or forwards data.
The public documentation covers user features and their access, state, and resource endpoints. Device administration, beta-only features, diagnostic logs, and internal maintenance endpoints aren't included, and beta-only chat debugging fields aren't part of the public contract.
Requires a pairing signature. Feature availability follows the capabilities returned by /data/user/system.
Interpret the documented status and result fields: HTTP 200 may mean read, save, or command enqueue; 202 means accepted. Neither alone proves playback or rendering completion. code is a machine error identifier (some older endpoints return only message/error); diagnostic text is not a stable enum. Do not blindly retry writes. Field descriptions define time and size units; missing, null, zero, and empty string are distinct.

request_id, slot, input, and output are required. input.type supports text, image_text, device_microphone, audio_file, and audio_stream; output.speech supports none, device, and client. Text, device recording, and audio streams use JSON; images and WAV use multipart. audio_stream requires little-endian PCM16, 16 kHz, mono, and audio.container=raw. For stream input or client output, connect to the turn’s /v1/ws/chat/turns/<turn_id>/audio WebSocket with a signed GET within 15 seconds of creation and wait for ready before sending audio. Client output uses MP3, WAV, or Ogg Opus according to the actual TTS metadata; after audio.end, acknowledge the final sequence before the turn can complete. Disconnecting ends the turn; resuming or replaying audio after reconnecting is unsupported. Files are limited to 1 MiB; WAV and stream input are limited to 30 seconds. slot must be the current slot, and existing conversation admission rules apply. 202 only means accepted. Retries with the same credentials, request_id, and request content reuse the original turn; conflicting content returns 409. Up to 256 turns are kept for 30 minutes after reaching a terminal state; idempotency records are lost on restart. input/complete and cancel use empty bodies to end recording or stream input and cancel the whole turn, respectively. When retention is not none, text and image-with-text input save the user message before acceptance; user_chat_ids contains the saved IDs. Microphone, WAV, and stream IDs may appear after transcription. interrupt defaults to true; false fails the turn with DEVICE_BUSY when the device is busy and retracts any user records written for this turn. retention defaults to full: save chat and update conversation state, summaries, long-term memory, and diaries; chat saves chat only; none saves neither chat nor images and makes none of those updates, leaving both chat_ids arrays empty. All modes read existing history and memory; the turn itself remains temporarily in memory.
Turn resources are visible only to their creating pairing credentials. turn_id is the server task ID; request_id is the client idempotency key. post.description:
Actions: PLAY, PAUSE, STOP, PREVIOUS, NEXT, SELECT_TRACK, QUERY_STATE, SEEK, SET_VOLUME, SET_PLAY_MODE, SET_SOUND_EFFECT and EDIT_QUEUE. The JSON body is limited to 1 MiB. source is LOCAL_TF; switch Bluetooth through /music/source. queue is allowed only with PLAY, SELECT_TRACK or EDIT_QUEUE and requires expected_queue_revision. EDIT_QUEUE replaces the current queue, without editing saved playlists or TF files. Clearing stops playback; removing a playing entry advances; editing while paused does not start playback. The device music page must be open except for QUERY_STATE, SET_VOLUME and SET_SOUND_EFFECT; otherwise HTTP 409 MODE_INACTIVE is returned. HTTP 200 means queued only. Match request_id in /music/playback or music_playback and inspect applied, error_code and the actual state. QUEUE_CONFLICT is an asynchronous execution result, not this endpoint's HTTP 409. request_id does not deduplicate commands. STOP clears the current track and retains the queue.
volume_level uses normalized 0–100 volume; volume_max is 100 when the device is ready. SEEK accepts progress_ms (milliseconds) or progress_ratio (0–1); send one. play_mode is sequence (repeat the queue in order), single_loop or shuffle; sound_effect is classical, surround or vocal. SELECT_TRACK accepts track_id or queue_entry_id; the entry ID takes precedence if both are sent. SELECT_TRACK with track_id and without queue or queue_entry_id installs the track's folder as the current queue. Use queue_entry_id to select within the existing queue. PLAY without a target resumes the current entry; an empty queue may be initialized from device files. The queue is an independent playback snapshot; later saved-playlist edits do not change it. status is IDLE, LOADING, PLAYING, PAUSED, COMPLETED or FAILED. version tracks snapshot changes and music_session_version tracks playback sessions; both are runtime values. applied confirms device execution, not a rendered frame. Natural completion is also sent as music_track_ended; polling can miss transient COMPLETED snapshots.

post.description: Reads text aloud directly in the current character's voice, without calling an LLM or writing to chat history. The JSON body requires request_id (UUID), slot (the current slot, 1 to 5), and text (1 to 16000 characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace). The body is limited to 128 KiB, and unknown fields are rejected. The device must be unlocked and meet the current interaction environment, page, and conversation admission rules. Interaction with the screen off follows the current device policy; screen_on alone does not determine admission. Existing interruption rules apply. 202 only means the request was accepted; use GET with utterance_id to check queued/synthesizing/playing/completed/failed/cancelled/cancelling. completed requires both synthesis and device playback to finish. cancel uses an empty body and only cancels tasks created with the same credentials. Retrying with the same credentials, request_id, and content returns the original task (200); different content returns 409. request_id shares a namespace with chat. Tasks and chat turns share a cache of up to 256 entries, terminal states are kept for 30 minutes, and a service restart clears them. Invalid credentials, switching users or characters, or clearing history ends tasks or makes them inaccessible. No audio file or audio stream is returned. A task enters playing only when your CODE27 confirms that playback started for the current playback stream; when animations are allowed, one Talking animation is chosen at random. A task can last up to 180 seconds.

post.description: Prepare reference audio → upload for preview → confirm to activate. Upload success does not apply the voice to a character. Use an allowed voice_id slot from 21–25 and a valid group_key. confirm.apply defaults to false; true applies it to the current character. Cloud confirmation can succeed while character application fails with 409 VOICE_CLONE_APPLY_FAILED; this does not roll back confirmation. Returned session_id identifies cloud processing, not pairing; audio_base64 contains preview audio. PUT /voice_clone/display_name updates an existing clone’s local name (at most 32 characters); an empty string restores its default number. Names are shared across language groups of the same provider, persist after restart, and are removed when the clone is deleted. They are not synced to the cloud. GET /voice_clone/quota requires the selected group_key and reads quota without consuming it. remaining_clone_count is the remaining monthly confirmation count; -1 or absent means unlimited. Only MiniMax uses quota; Qwen Audio does not. READY does not consume quota; use the cloud value after ACTIVATED. Deletion does not refund quota. Exhaustion returns HTTP 429, code=VOICE_CLONE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED and data.remaining_clone_count=0. Localize errors by code without matching message text; unknown codes use a generic retry message.

events.lifecycle: ready contains protocol_version=v1 and no business data. subscribe replaces the complete set; [] cancels all. Deduplicate names; unknown names reject the whole request. Result precedes new topics; retained topics are not initialized again. topic_error SERVICE_NOT_READY affects one topic; resubmit to retry. Reconnect restores subscriptions before HTTP recovery. History preserves its ordered 128-change window, then sync; track-ended uses a 64-event window with no replay across disconnects. Unsubscribed providers do no work.
